articles.title: NBA Updates 2027-28 Salary Cap Projections, Full Details Revealed in New Rumors
articles.summary: The NBA reportedly informed teams of updated salary cap projections for the 2027-28 season on Saturday.
articles.body:
The NBA reportedly informed teams of updated salary cap projections for the 2027-28 season on Saturday.

According to Fred Katz of The Athletic, the 2027-28 season is expected to contain a $176 million salary cap as well as a $213 million luxury tax line.

The NBA previously projected a $174 million cap and a $234 million second apron for the league's 2027-28 campaign on June 30, per Mike Vorkunov of The Athletic.

Ranking the NBA's Top 10 Trade Targets 🎯

As for the upcoming 2026-27 season, the salary cap is set at $164.96 million with a luxury tax level at $200.43 million.

During the previous 2025-26 season, NBA teams operated with a $154.65 million salary cap to go along with a $187.9 million tax level.

Although the exact 2027-28 salary cap won't become official until June 2027, teams can continue to build their rosters with the reported updated projections in mind.

That could include front offices attempting to restructure their rosters in order to avoid crossing the $213 million luxury tax line and the penalties associated with it.

26 of the league's 30 teams currently have over $213 million in total cap allocations for their 2027-28 campaigns (via Spotrac ). The 30 organizations also have an average of $240.8 million in 2027-28 total cap allocations.

In the meantime, the 2026-27 season will begin on Oct. 20.

articles.title: They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets
articles.summary: Some people fired in the wake of Kirk's assassination have won big settlements from employers, others have had to start over from scratch.
articles.body:
Watch: These Americans were fired for posting about Charlie Kirk

In September 2025, Gerald Bourguet felt he was finally living his dream life: he and his wife had bought a house with a pool, they had just welcomed a baby boy, and he was writing about professional men's basketball as his full-time job.

But all of that changed after he made a series of online posts critical of the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk hours after he was fatally shot on 10 September, while speaking on the campus of Utah Valley University.

In the posts, Bourguet described Kirk as an "evil man" and suggested he had dedicated his life to hateful causes. He also criticised Kirk's supporters saying they had not been vocal about school shootings.

"I had seen the way that people were talking about this person - kind of eulogising him and lionising him and it bothered me based on a lot of the things that he had said," Bourguet told the BBC.

Kirk, who founded Christian youth organisation Turning Point USA, was a divisive figure in US politics. For many on the political right, he was charismatic and had a unique skill in making conservative ideas appeal to young people. But for his opponents, his comments on a large swathe of issues from race to immigration, gun control and gender identity were deeply offensive.

Screenshots of Bourguet's critical posts went viral quickly. He was fired from his job, his address was exposed online, and he began receiving threatening text messages, he said. Concerned for their safety, the family fled the state with their four-month-old. They returned months later to sell the house and permanently relocated.

A year later, he says he doesn't regret what he said, but acknowledged: "My life will never be the same after this".

"At age 35, I am having to start over in a lot of respects… I wouldn't wish this on my worst enemy," Bourguet said from his new location, which the BBC agreed not to disclose.

PHNX Sports, Bourguet's former employer, did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

Bourguet was one of hundreds fired or disciplined over critical comments of Kirk after his death. While some of those who have lost their jobs have been reinstated or received restitution - sometimes in the millions - others like Bourguet have had to rebuild from scratch.

In the aftermath of Kirk's assassination, most people kept their feelings to themselves, or shared them with close friends.

But on polarised social media, people rushed to laude, or denounce, the controversial activist. Some called the criticisms, posted hours after his death, tasteless. But others called for swift action, arguing they were callous, mocking, and could even incite further violence.

Laura Loomer, an influential right-wing commentator with nearly 2 million followers on X, warned Kirk's critics to "prepare to have your whole future professional aspirations ruined".

The push for punishment also came from the highest levels of US government.

"When you see someone celebrating Charlie's murder, call them out," Vice-President JD Vance said days after the assassination. "And hell, call their employer," he added.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told the BBC: "Anyone who engages in or endorses political violence or assassination culture must be condemned in the harshest terms possible."

Critics on the left said there was a difference between criticism of Kirk and celebrating his death. Some accused these conservative leaders of hypocrisy, as many had previously bemoaned the rise of "cancel culture" – where people who voice controversial opinions face severe consequences at work and socially.

"Cancel culture can be good, it's bad when it's applied in the wrong ways," Jordan Pace, a Republican member of the South Carolina House of Representatives, told the BBC. "If you are someone who celebrates political assassinations and the murder of an innocent man with two young children in a way that many people did, then yeah, that's an appropriate way for society to function, to shame those people."

Pace had previously called for defunding universities in his state if they didn't take actions against employees who made comments about Kirk. One of his posts was re-shared by US President Donald Trump.

Across the nation, some employers – private and public – acted swiftly to the pressure campaign. Reliable figures on the number of people fired or disciplined are hard to come by, but a Reuters tally last November found more than 600 instances. It is likely an under-count because not all cases received national or local press attention.

The specific actions that led to these disciplinary decisions run the gamut. In Tennessee, anthropology professor Tamar Shirinian was suspended and later fired for a Facebook comment saying "the world is better off" without Kirk.

A Delta Air Lines flight attendant was fired after posting "good riddance" in response to Kirk's killing. Office Depot supply store fired an employee for refusing to serve a customer who had wanted to print flyers for a Kirk vigil. Delta Air Lines declined to comment. Office Depot did not respond to a request for comment.

Others were disciplined even if they did not make any direct comments about Kirk or his death. Darren Michael, a theatre professor in Tennessee, was fired after he posted a screenshot of a news article from 2023, that covered Kirk's controversial speech on gun control. In the article, Kirk is quoted saying protecting citizens' rights to own guns was worth it even if it led to some gun deaths every year.

Florida's Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission fired biologist Brittney Brown after she reposted a meme that also satirised Kirk's position on gun violence in light of his own shooting.

"I was absolutely gutted," Brown said about her firing to the BBC. "It was like the entire world just completely flipped on its head in a moment."

Lawsuits have yielded big pay outs for those fired

In the year since Kirk's killing, dozens of lawsuits have been filed across the country by people fired for their comments about the activist, arguing their terminations violated their rights to free speech. The suits have led to substantial pay outs in some cases.

Brown agreed to a $485,000 (£355,000) financial settlement – about 12 times Brown's annual salary.

Darren Michael was reinstated by the Austin Peay State University and in January, the school agreed to pay him $500,000 to settle legal claims. The school did not respond to a request for comment.

In the largest settlement reviewed by the BBC, the University of Tennessee agreed to pay $1.9m to resolve a lawsuit brought by anthropologist Tamar Shirinian, over her "better off" comment. As part of the settlement, she will not be reinstated and has agreed not to reapply for future positions at the school.

Recently, an arbitrator ordered The Washington Post to rehire, with back pay, opinion journalist Karen Attiah, who was fired for her online posts that said in part she was not going to engage in "performative mourning for a white man that espoused violence".

Several other lawsuits remain pending, the BBC found.

Most of the legal actions have been pursued by employees of government institutions, or unionised workers, who have some free-speech protections.

But in the US, most private sector employees work under "at-will" contracts, which means they can be can be fired without reason.

Even those who have scored some victories don't see it as a win.

"All I wanted was my job back," biologist Brown said. "How much taxpayer money did they waste on this when I barely made $40,000 a year? So no, it does not feel like justice."

Shirinian told the BBC she too had wanted to return to her job but felt a legal case could be a lengthy affair.

"I took a settlement because this allows me to move on with my life," she told the BBC. "The one small regret that I have is that I will not see my day in court and justice will not be served in that way. But I think that the number of the settlement actually speaks to that anyway."

The University of Tennessee and Florida's Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

As an at-will employee at a private company, Bourguet is unlikely to prevail in a lawsuit challenging his dismissal. A year on, he said he has struggled to find work. The new state he lives in has a professional basketball team, but he believes the ordeal has made him unemployable in the small world of sports writers. Instead, he's started his own podcast, although he doubts he can earn enough through it to pay the bills.

"I have accepted that that life is over and that I need to start a new one." Leaving the country is now on the table, he said.

Despite the huge personal and professional costs, those who spoke to the BBC said after months of reflection, they did not regret their actions.

"I have a right to say what I want to say," Brown said. "They are the ones who should have the regrets, not me," she said referring to her former employer.

Shirinian apologised to the university days after her suspension. She told the BBC her comment was "an emotional outburst" that was not intended to be public and that she regretted the tone used.

"I don't regret the sentiment, however" she said, adding "the sentiment was that I am not sad. And I refuse to be made to feel like I have to be sad that someone who was so hateful was killed".

Bourguet also said he does not regret his comments although he has conflicting thoughts about its consequences.

"I don't regret that line of thinking because I think it's important to push back on things that are steeped in hatred," he said, referring to Kirk's political message.

"I don't regret what I said. I don't regret the way that I said it. I do regret the ripple effects that came from it and the way that they impacted me, my career, my family, and my son."

articles.title: El objetivo de España en el Mundial sigue vivo: ganar una medalla
articles.standfirst: Juega por el bronce mundial ante Alemania este domingo a las 16.30
articles.summary: Juega por el bronce mundial ante Alemania este domingo a las 16.30
articles.body: España va a tener menos de 24 horas (18 exactamente, 16.30 h de este domingo) para cambiar la decepción por la derrota ante Estados Unidos por motivación y combustible para el partido ante Alemania. Conociendo al entrenador, a las jugadoras e incluso a la gente de la FEB que rodea al equipo, eso no va a ser un problema. La selección estuvo muy cerca de ganar a EEUU. Realmente más cerca que nunca porque nunca se había perdido por tan poco en partido oficial con las estadounidenses. Son 12 de 12, pero en ese tramo hubo dos derrotas por 13 puntos. En Berlín se cayó por 10, aunque la sensación es que los dos equipos estaban más cerca todavía. La desazón en la expedición española sobre todo es pensar que se ha perdido una ocasión histórica. La parte positiva, es que el equipo no va a dejar de crecer. España quería luchar por el oro y se perdió. Pero no hay que perder la perspectiva. En su presentación, todos hablaron de traerse una medalla, así que ese objetivo sigue vivo, intacto y al alcance de la mano de las jugadoras de Miguel Méndez. Este domingo una cita con la historia espera a la selección. Tiene tres medallas mundiales en su colección, la plata de Turquía en 2014 y los bronces de la República Checa en 2010 y de Tenerife en 2018. Puestos a pensar el resultado de Berlín es brutal pase lo que pase: cuarta vez que España se mete entre las cuatro mejores del Mundial en sus últimas cinco ediciones, y eso que la de 2022 no la jugó. Si sube al podio sería una hazaña, el cuarto en cinco Mundiales. Miguel Méndez decía tras el partido ante EEUU que apenas tendrán tiempo para preparar el partido. Eso es una constante en este Mundial en el que se ha puesto a prueba la capacidad de los entrenadores para poder trabajar adecuadamente con sus equipos. Mucho mérito para los técnicos que han tenido que trabajar en el alambre entre jugadoras llegando a última hora, procesos de preparación incompletos y las zancadillas de la FIBA con pocos descansos y partidos muy seguidos. España se enfrenta a un rival al que ha ganado en dos ocasiones muy seguidas. Primero en la preparación, 60-65, en tierras germanas, en un partido con muchas bajas, y luego en la fase de grupos, en el partido inaugural, 83-53, cuando pocos se imaginaban que Alemania seguiría jugando hasta este domingo. Méndez no quiere ni oír hablar de esos partidos, no se parecerán en nada al de la final por el bronce ante un equipo que viene de subidón tras su victoria ante Bélgica. Alemania viene de la nada al todo, y de los dos equipos derrotados el sábado, es la que menos impacto psicológico tuvo. Su papel, sea cual sea el resultado final, es brillante. Querrán ganar el bronce, pero ya han ganado aunque lo pierdan. Ofensivamente el equipo germano carbura con los puntos de Frieda Buhner (12,7), Marie Guelich (11,8) y Leo Fiebich (9,8). Son el segundo equipo que mejor rebotea (45,6, seis rebotes más que España) sólo por detrás de Estados Unidos, y son el sexto mejor anotador del campeonato, justo por detrás de la selección. En valoración son cuartas (92,2), por delante de España, quintas (90,4). Alemania es un equipo que se ha ido entonando a lo largo del campeonato hasta acabarlo en el mejor estado de forma posible. Además tendrán un pabellón repleto (en la semifinal ante Francia tenían todas las entradas vendidas) apoyando a un equipo que busca el primer tesoro mundial de su historia. El seleccionador dijo que tratarán de cambiar las caras de tristeza por la alegría que se merecen estas jugadoras por el canpeonato que han hecho. Que así sea.

articles.title: Arch Manning and Texas Longhorns erase 20-point deficit to stun Ohio State in shocking comeback for the ages
articles.summary: Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns erased a 23-3 deficit against Ohio State in a stunning fourth-quarter surge that silenced doubters on a wild day.
articles.body: AUSTIN, TX - Well, I don't know if Texas is back, but they darn sure made a statement on Saturday night against No. 1 Ohio State in one of the craziest college football games in recent memory. Actually, this was about as ugly as it could get for the No. 4 Longhorns football program, at least for three quarters of this thriller. For a year, we had been looking forward to this rematch between two of the top-spenders in college football, with Texas spending around $40 million on its roster this season. Saturday night did not disappoint. TEXAS VS OHIO STATE IS MORE THAN A REMATCH: A BBQ-FUELED COLLISION BETWEEN COLLEGE FOOTBALL POWER BROKERS Led by Cam Coleman, Trey Wingo and a flurry of offensive weapons, the Longhorns looked more like a mediocre football team for three quarters. Then the Buckeyes could no longer convert, allowing Texas to take advantage of a worn-down Ohio State team. The first offensive play of the game for Texas turned into a fumble. From there, Ohio State toyed with the Longhorns throughout the first half. The Buckeyes led 20-3 at halftime after holding Texas to just 97 yards of offense over the first 30 minutes. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This was the Jeremiah Smith show, with the Ohio State wide receiver making Texas’ secondary look inept almost every time quarterback Julian Sayin looked his way, at least until it wasn’t. For Arch Manning, there was nothing much going his way for three quarters of this Top-5 showdown, which had the Longhorns trailing 23-3. Whether it was overthrown passes, dropped dimes or interesting play calls from the offensive staff, this one was looking like a major letdown. Game lived up to the hype in the fourth quarter, while both teams look flawed At the 8:55 mark of the third quarter, Jeremiah Smith darted down the sidelines as Julian Sayin threw up a heave in front of the Texas Longhorns bench. There was only one way this one was going to end, and it came with Smith dogging a defender in the process of bringing down the 48-yard catch. How many NFL receivers are better than Jeremiah right now? Maybe five? But the star wideout couldn’t do it all, and Texas’ relentless fourth-quarter performance will be remembered for years to come. There have been close and thrilling games before, but this felt more like Texas finally getting a massive monkey off its back. Finally, the Longhorns had won a game with their backs against the wall. ARCH MANNING ISN’T BACKING DOWN FROM EXPECTATIONS, AND NEITHER IS STEVE SARKISIAN, AS CFP SEMIS AREN'T ENOUGH At long last, Steve Sarkisian won a heavyweight fight at home, with so much pressure on the program to take the next step. "What it can do is this team can understand that we can overcome adversity, and we're going to get faced with more adversity," Sarkisian said postgame. "Hopefully, this serves as a lesson that we can come back from a lot." Who would have thought at the 6:13 mark of the third quarter that we would be discussing a Longhorns win that could propel the program moving forward? No more excuses for Texas, or Arch Manning Just like everyone else across the country, folks are sick of hearing about whether or not Texas is "back." But, this one is not going to sit well with those around college football who are already sick of hearing about the Texas Longhorns. As Arch Manning wrapped up his postgame interview with ESPN, the Longhorns quarterback darted towards the Texas student section like a kid on Christmas. After coming up short last season, along with the pressure that came with being the leader on a team with such high expectations, it felt as though Manning finally let out a giant sigh of relief. He took pictures, donned a cowboy hat, sang with his teammates and ran towards his coaches. Manning's Texas teammates came rushing to him, overjoyed with emotion after what they had just helped the Longhorns accomplish. Not much can beat this night, besides maybe winning an SEC or CFP title. As the smoke started pluming from the field, athletic director Chris Del Conte walked over to SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, who was waiting to head toward the Texas locker room to celebrate the win with Longhorns' faithful. Parents were taking pictures with their kids on the field. Even Ted Cruz walked back onto the playing surface to celebrate the warranted jinx that he had supposedly put on this team by showing up for recent game days in the past. There were moments late in the third quarter where Arch Manning brought the crowd to its feet, thanks to his scrambling throughout the field. Capped off by a touchdown near the start of the fourth quarter, the Longhorns provided fans with hope, and that's all they needed during this crazy night. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER On Saturday night, we witnessed one of the wildest games in recent memory. We witnessed a potential Texas revival, with a deflating loss for an Ohio State that lost its way thanks to a Longhorns defense that finally rose to the occasion in the second half. What happens next? Maybe a rematch in the College Football Playoff? Who knows. But on Saturday night in Austin, it was the Texas Longhorns who finally took the next regular season step that its fans were praying for.

articles.title: Kate Koval: Ukrainian player transfers from LSU to Baylor after Russia controversy
articles.summary: Ukrainian basketball player Kate Koval has been granted a transfer waiver to join Baylor University after leaving Lousiana State because they signed a Russian player.
articles.body:
Ukrainian basketball player Kate Koval has joined a new college team after leaving Louisiana State University because they had signed a Russian player.

Koval, 20, was granted a transfer waiver by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) at the request of LSU.

The waiver allowed Koval to join a new team despite the transfer window closing in April, and she has signed with Baylor University in Texas.

Koval played in all 35 of LSU's matches last season, averaging 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game.

But following the arrival of 17-year-old Anna Minaeva, it was announced that Koval had departed for "personal reasons" after her first season.

Koval then said that Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine was why she stepped away.

"My father serves in the Ukrainian military and takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression," she wrote on Instagram.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract. People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes.

"The timing of this situation and the deep personal effect it has had on me, my family and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me."

Student athletes can only be granted transfer waivers outside the window by the NCAA for extenuating circumstances or events unrelated to the sport that are out of the individual's control.

The event must have occurred after the student-athlete's most recent opportunity to be entered into the NCAA transfer portal had closed.

BBC Sport has contacted LSU to confirm under which terms the waiver was requested.

articles.title: Predicting the Top 10 Scorers for the 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: The NBA discourse needs a break from cap-circumvention scandals and its various prediction-market entanglements, which means it's time to talk buckets.
articles.body:
The NBA discourse needs a break from cap-circumvention scandals and its various prediction-market entanglements, which means it's time to talk buckets.

Chances are, you fell in love with the game because a player you liked scored a bunch of points in a game you happened to be watching. Let's acknowledge the purity of that experience by turning our full attention to something simple and undeniably fun.

That's right: It's time to predict the top 10 scorers for the upcoming 2026-27 season.

10. Donovan Mitchell, Cleveland Cavaliers

Peyton Watson's potential as an on-ball weapon is purely additive for the title-chasing Cleveland Cavaliers. It's not going to chip away at Donovan Mitchell's first-option reps.

Last year's 27.9 points per game might still be out of reach if Watson eats up some possessions, or if Evan Mobley takes another step as a creator. But Mitchell has topped 24.0 points per game every year since 2019-20 and feels highly likely to do so again.

Remember, if guys like Watson and Mobley (and James Harden) are dangerous enough to command more defensive attention, Mitchell could benefit. He shot 40.7 percent on catch-and-shoot threes during the regular season but attempted just 231 such shots, ranking outside the league's top 75 .

If defenses have to account for other threats, that number could rise along with Mitchell's scoring efficiency. If he loses anything in volume, that should make up for it.

Deni Avdija proved himself as a first-option shot creator for the first time last season, averaging 24.1 points per game on the strength of a brutally forceful downhill driving game.

A ruggedly strong 6'8", Avdija bull rushes opponents and then hits them with one of the league's best slow-step packages. Compromised by his strength, defenders were routinely off balance and out of position, allowing Avdija to amass 9.2 free-throw attempts per game.

The Portland Trail Blazers roster is overloaded with guards, but none of them deserves to take touches away from Avdija—not after he barged into his first All-Star game and added a career-high 6.7 assists per contest to his profile. If anything, the Blazers should lean even harder on their best player going forward.

If Avdija comes closer to matching 2023-24's 37.4 percent from three after last year's disappointing 31.8 percent clip, defenders who have no choice but to be on their heels will pay for sagging off of him. Entering his prime years, Avdija comes with a 25.0-point-per-game floor.

The Detroit Pistons didn't find a capable secondary creator over the offseason, but they surrounded Cade Cunningham with shooting.

Isaiah Joe, John Collins, Taurean Prince and Gary Harris were all above 40.0 percent from deep last season and should keep the floor spaced for Detroit's superstar. They won't, however, lighten the playmaking load. Add those two expectations together, and the result might be a higher-scoring version of Cunningham who is perfectly positioned to get more of his own buckets than ever.

Cunningham ranked fifth in drives per game last year, but generated the fewest free-throw attempts and shot t he worst percentage in those situations of anyone else in the top five. Better spacing should widen his avenues of attack, creating more chances to finish at the rim or draw a foul.

Cunningham's previous career high is 26.1 points per game, set in 2024-25. He's going to top that with ease.

The Boston Celtics employed a single-star approach last season, and it produced a career year for Jaylen Brown. Why shouldn't the process repeat itself with a healthy Jayson Tatum in place of the departed Brown?

The Celtics replaced Brown, who put up at least 17.0 shots per game every year since 2020-21, with Paul George, who hasn't averaged more than 17.0 shots per game since 2021-22. Even if George stays healthy, a large share of the shots and on-ball reps that once went to Brown will fall to Tatum.

Both intuition and statistical history say that'll result in more touches and points. Tatum's usage rate in 102 career games without Brown is 31.2 percent, and he averages 26.3 points per game. In 499 games with his former teammate, those figures were a 28.2 usage rate and 23.0 points per contest.

Nikola Jokić has averaged between 24.5 and 29.7 points per game over the last six seasons, and the continued degradation of his surrounding talent points to him clocking in toward the higher end of that spread in 2026-27.

Peyton Watson is gone via a sign-and-trade, making it two straight offseasons that the Denver Nuggets have downgraded their supporting cast for financial reasons. Though Watson's exit won't hurt Denver's scoring as much as Michael Porter Jr.'s departure last summer, Jokić still figures to carry at least as much of the scoring burden as he did in 2025-26.

DeMar DeRozan is still in the league because he can get buckets, but he profiles as a second-unit weapon.

Jokić registered a career high in free-throw attempts per game last season, which shows he's still finding new ways to exploit defenders. Don't rule out more growth in that area, increased three-point volume or new wrinkles to his mid-post game. Players with his level of talent and feel are always adding dimensions.

It sounds strange to say about a player whose newest star teammate once scored 83 points in a game, but Giannis Antetokounmpo is used to being surrounded by a bit more offensive punch.

Damian Lillard was a major source of points when healthy, and the combination of Khris Middleton and Jrue Holiday offered strong support before that brief two-star era.

Bam Adebayo has never been a score-first threat and peaked at 20.4 points per game in 2022-23. Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson are past their primes. Davion Mitchell is in the league because of his defense. The list goes on.

Antetokounmpo fell below 30.0 points per game for the first time since 2021-22 last season. He'll be motivated to prove he's still a first-tier MVP candidate after a messy exit from Milwaukee, and he may also need to reach new scoring heights just for the Miami Heat offense to function.

Though he'll always be defined by his defensive impact, Victor Wembanyama showed enough last season to suggest he has massive upside as a scorer.

The San Antonio Spurs still don't seem to have a handle on the best way to use Wemby, too often tasking him with creating plays from the perimeter rather than making him a finisher on spot-ups, post-ups or hard rolls to the rim. Once they dial in the correct usage mix for Wembanyama, the sky's the limit.

Don't forget the likelihood of a generational mega-talent improving in his age-23 season. Wembanyama could juice his three-point accuracy, get to the foul line more often or dominate the offensive glass for put-backs as he adds strength.

Even if the Spurs simply keep Wemby in the same suboptimal role, the potential for him to crack 30.0 points per game remains high because he produced a historically unusual scoring average for a player logging fewer than 30 minutes per game.

Among players who averaged fewer than 30 minutes per game and appeared in at least 50 contests, Wemby's 2025-26 scoring average of 25.0 points per game was the highest of all time .

3. Anthony Edwards, Minnesota Timberwolves

Two factors work in favor of Anthony Edwards adding to last year's 28.8 points per game, which would put him in a great position to collect his first scoring title.

The first is that Ant has made a habit of getting better in every season of his career. His scoring average and true shooting percentage have trended up in each of his six years as a pro. At this point, if you're not expecting continued offensive growth from the 25-year-old superstar, you're ignoring a very compelling pattern.

Edwards' newest teammate is far from a perfect player, but Ball has a history of making the scorers around him much more efficient. Last year, Ball's Charlotte teammates saw their collective true shooting percentage climb by nine points when sharing the floor with the pass-happy point guard. Edwards is bound to enjoy some of the same benefits.

2. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Oklahoma City Thunder

If you had to bet on one player to average at least 30.0 points per game this season, it'd have to be Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. He's crested that mark for four straight seasons, and the league probably didn't figure out how to stop him over the summer.

SGA combines unsurpassed scoring craft, disorienting change-of-pace, elite accuracy on short jumpers and has suckered defenders into fouls better than anyone in the league. He's led the NBA in free throws made per game every year since 2023-24.

Last year's 59.7 effective field-goal percentage was the highest of Gilgeous-Alexander's career, suggesting he's not done adding layers to his game.

The only thing preventing SGA from ranking first on this list is his measured approach to the game. Other scorers are insatiable, hungry for as many buckets as they can get. Gilgeous-Alexander isn't quite that greedy, finishing sixth last year in field-goal attempts per 36 minutes.

He scores only as much as his team needs him to.

The Los Angeles Lakers removed a high-volume scorer from the picture by letting LeBron James go and effectively replaced him with big man Walker Kessler, creating a perfect scenario for Luka Dončić's scoring potential.

Dončić led the league at 33.5 points per game last season, but that fell short of his career high of 33.9 in 2023-24. In addition to health, Dončić had a pair of rim-running bigs sopping up most of the center minutes with that Dallas Mavericks team. Dereck Lively II dunked 52.7 percent of his field-goal attempts in 2023-24, and Daniel Gafford slammed 46.2 percent of his.

When Dončić has a lob threat to draw in the defense, it supercharges his own scoring in the lane.

DeAndre Ayton and his career 15.5 percent dunk attempt rate were of little help a year ago, but Kessler's career figure of 34.2 percent comes much closer to the Lively-Gafford number that unlocked the highest-scoring version of Dončić we've ever seen.

articles.title: El Barça gana la Liga Catalana pero se le llena la enfermería: ya van tres lesionados
articles.standfirst: Los azulgranas se imponen en la final al iLerna Lleida (96-87), pero Brizuela se retira lesionado y se suma a Evboumwan y Makoundou
articles.summary: Los azulgranas se imponen en la final al iLerna Lleida (96-87), pero Brizuela se retira lesionado y se suma a Evboumwan y Makoundou
articles.body: El Barça ha ganado este domingo la Lliga Catalana de baloncesto tras vencer al Ilerna Lleida por 96-87 en la final disputada en el Palau d'Esports Catalunya de Tarragona ante 4.300 espectadores. El partido se resolvió en el último cuarto, cuando el Barça, que había ido por detrás en el marcador prácticamente desde el inicio, apretó y consiguió una victoria muy trabajada, liderada, sobre todo, por el escolta Kevin Punter y el alero Joel Parra. Los dos equipos salieron imprecisos y el Barça aprovechó su poderío en la pintura para llevar la iniciativa en el marcador en los primeros compases. Una canasta de Punter puso a los de Aleksander Sekulic 6 arriba (15-9), pero la entrada de Ejim cambió la dinámica. El ala-pívot canadiense anotó dos triples consecutivos para igualar el choque y el Lleida encadenó un parcial de 0-14 para ponerse 8 puntos por delante (15-23). El Ilerna Lleida, que en los dos partidos de la fase de grupos había ido siempre a remolque en la primera mitad, comenzó la final dominando a un Barça sin ideas en ataque y con porcentajes muy bajos de acierto en el tiro. Joel Parra cortó la sequía culé con un triple prácticamente sobre la bocina. En el segundo cuarto, el Barça subió un punto la intensidad, pero el Lleida no se amilanó y, liderado por Mcghee y Perrin, mantuvo el control e incluso amplió su ventaja (30-38). Los azulgranas, a trompicones, se encomendaron al acierto desde fuera del perímetro de Gibson y Umude para equilibrar el encuentro, pero, lastrados por las pérdidas de balón, no conseguían coger el pulso a la final. El Ilerna Lleida, más enchufado también en el rebote ofensivo, fue mejor en la primera mitad y se marchó al descanso con una ligera ventaja de 4 puntos (40-44). Era el primer partido de esta Lliga Catalana en el que los de Gerard Encuentra se iban al vestuario por delante. El tercer cuarto empezó igual, con el Lleida más fino en el tiro y el Barça perdido en pista. Sekulic aún no ha conseguido engranar todas las piezas de un equipo con muchas caras nuevas. Una falta flagrante de Martin permitió a Lleida anotar 5 puntos consecutivos (dos tiros libres de Ejim y un triple de Mcghee) y alcanzar una máxima ventaja de nueve puntos (53-62). El Barça, cargado de fatas personales, se mantenía en el partido gracias al talento individual de Punter y Robinson. Además, perdió a Brirzuela, lesionado a falta de 51 segundos para terminar el tercer parcial. Se retiró cojeando y hay preocupación en el equipo azulgrana, pues su lesión se suma a las de Tosan Evboumwan y Yoan Makoundou. El último cuarto arrancó un ajustado 66-69 en favor del Ilerna Lleida. Parra cogió las riendas del Barça y con dos triples puso a su equipo por delante (72-71). El partido empezó a decantarse del lado azulgrana. Los de Sekulic, con una gran defensa, desactivaron al Lleida en ataque e imprimieron más velocidad al juego. Un triple de Punter puso a los culés 8 por delante (83-75) a falta de cinco minutos. El Barça ya no se dejó sorprender y controló el choque hasta el final. Se impuso por 9 puntos (96-87) y alzó su 26ª Lliga Catalana. El azulgrana Robinson fue nombrado mejor jugador del torneo. 96. Ilerna Lleida (23+21+25+18): Mcghee (18), Hughes (9), Rodríguez (4), Sanz (4), Perrin (16) -cinco inicial-, Batemon (12), Ejim (14), Paulí (-), Shurna (5), Majauskas (5), Torrens (-) y Pou (-). Árbitros: Óscar Perea, Jordi Aliaga y Alberto Baena. Eliminaron con cinco faltas a Ejim (min.40). articles.title: Dan Dakich says women might be the reason for Nike's downfall: 'They p----d them off'
articles.summary: Dan Dakich says Nike's collapse stems from alienating women buyers and losing ground to Athleta and Lululemon in a booming competitive market.
articles.body: It's no secret at this point that Nike is taking a nosedive. They're being mercilessly mocked online for releasing a low-effort series of NBA jerseys, and their stock has plummeted so much that they are set to get the boot from the S&P 100 later this month. While plenty of personalities have weighed in, OutKick's Dan Dakich decided to throw his hat in the ring and discuss just how bad things have gotten for the failing athletic apparel giant. OUTKICK'S CRAIG CARTON REVEALS THE REAL REASON NIKE STOCK IS IN THE TANK: 'THEY'RE FAILING MISERABLY' On a recent episode of his "Don't @ Me" show, Dakich was joined by Dan Zaksheske and Jason Hammer to break down the missteps committed by Nike that led them to this lowly state. Zaksheske opined that the "go woke, go broke" mantra certainly applies here, but we have to take everything into account, including complacency. "I would compare Nike to Disney," Zaksheske stated. "They're just resting on their laurels. They're not creating anything new." Hammer offered a different perspective, giving credit to FOX Business's Taylor Riggs for the insight. TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW "They gave a middle finger to the retailers," he said. "They thought they could go directly to the consumer and that didn't work, coming out of a COVID-era where people were desperate to actually go out and go to the stores, see the displays, and the Nike displays weren't there anymore." Dakich certainly agreed with his guests, but he offered his own take on the matter. "Local competition," he said when pointing a finger at Nike's problems. "Athleta is booming. Lululemon is booming. It used to be Nike or Adidas, which one are you going to buy?" Competition in the marketplace can either force you to improve or make you watch from the sidelines, and Nike seems to be doing the latter. Alienating the local retailers was a big mistake from Nike, but Dakich posits that the company has a female problem, too. "Women have said, 'Bulls---, don't insult us,'" Dakich said. "Who's buying stuff? It ain't me and it ain't you (Hammer)... it is freaking women, and (Nike) p----d them off." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. articles.title: Iyana Martín lidera a España al bronce en el inicio de una nueva era
articles.standfirst: Un equipo joven y con un talento formidable derrota a Alemania para volver al podio del Mundial
articles.summary: Un equipo joven y con un talento formidable derrota a Alemania para volver al podio del Mundial
articles.body: Y así, señoras y señores, chicos y chicas, es como irrumpe en la historia una generación de jugadoras que va a dominar el baloncesto femenino en los próximos años. España, después de estar fuera del último Mundial, gana en Berlín el bronce y aumenta su colección de premios en el torneo a cuatro (una plata y tres bronces). Pero lo más importante es que la selección, que para subir al podio ganó al anfitrión Alemania, 81-58, cuenta con un equipo extremadamente joven pero repleto de talento que regresado a la élite Mundial por la puerta grande. Pero sobre todo tiene a una jugadora que va a marcar una época. A sus 20 años Iyana Martín se ha convertido en una de las mejores jugadoras del Mundial, sólo superada por Gabby Williams en Francia. Ha estado muy por encima del nivel de cualquiera de las estrellas de EEUU, dominando cada partido. Lo hizo también ante Alemania con sus canastas, sus pases y lo mejor, su magia para mover y dirigir al equipo. Es pura fantasía. A pesar del marcador final, no fue un partido fácil para España, nada que ver con el de la primera fase en la que la salida de las de Méndez reventó el partido y no hubo respuestas por parte de las germanas. Esto era una final, por el bronce, en un repleto Uber Arena y mucho por jugar. Volvió España a tener una excelente puesta en escena y por eso gozó de la primera gran ventaja, 22-9, que se quedó en nada cuando Alemania igualó, 33-33, con cuatro minutos jugados del segundo cuarto. Otro parcial duro encajado por la selección, 11-24, en uno de los aspectos en los que más se ha notado quizá la falta de experiencia. Al final del segundo acto España mandaba pero por poco, 40-36. Era un partido en el que Méndez tenía que tener a todas enchufadas. Buenos minutos iniciales de Megan Gustafson y de María Conde. También de Elena Buenavida que sigue aportando cada vez que juega, aunque no se vea en las estadísticas. Aunque por encima estaban Iyana y su magia, y Raquel Carrera, especialmente inspirada. El tercer cuarto fue de España, fue cuando construyó la ventaja que le daría el bronce. El brutal parcial de 14-0 en cinco minutos (se pasó de un 50-39 a un 54-39 a 3:56), separó a los dos equipos en el marcador. De esos 14 puntos, Carrera firmó ocho en un tramo de juego memorable. Las alemanas apretaron al final del acto, pero sólo para quedarse a 10 puntos: 61-51. Con el marcador encarrilado, España salió mejor en el último cuarto y dos triples (Conde y Cazorla) establecían la máxima hasta ese momento (67-51). La medalla de bronce aparecía en el horizonte para que las jugadoras espeñolas la agarraran. Era el mínimo premio que merecían al fabuloso campeonato que habían realizado. Los últimos minutos del partido estaban completamente controlados por Iyana y la selección. Fue dejar pasar, segundo a segundo, un partido que las de Méndez no querían dejar de disfrutar. No era para menos, estaban firmando una histórica medalla, la cuarta de España, la primera de un equipo de ensueño. Iyana acabó con 22 puntos y 9 asistencias y no es la MVP del torneo porque no jujgó la final. Carrera hizo 15 y 5 rebotes, Conde aportó 12 y Fam, 10 con 7 rebotes. Otra jugadora que, como Iyana, comienza a sembrar una carrera en la selección absoluta con un bronce Mundial.

articles.title: FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis speaks out on Caitlin Clark's impact on growth of World Cup
articles.summary: FIBA's secretary general says Caitlin Clark and women's basketball stars could surpass male players in popularity at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
articles.body: FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis addressed the impact of Caitlin Clark and other new young players playing in the World Cup for the first time on the tournament's growth and visibility. Zagklis, speaking at a press conference before the World Cup Final against France, called Clark one of the biggest stars of her generation and predicted that the popularity of the women's basketball players could surpass the men's at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. "I think what these players, Caitlin, one of them, have done in increasing the popularity of the women's game is incredible. We should feel very proud about them. And I can tell you, me and my team have been supportive of what USA Basketball and each and every national member federation coming into the World Cup had planned for their promotion. And we tried to amplify that experience. They themselves, the players said this is a unique moment for them," Zagklis said. THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE "So while I may not be able to quantify the answer and give you exact numbers, but our team perhaps can do that after the tournament, I can tell you that the popularity of our women's game, of Caitlin as one of the biggest stars, not the biggest star of this generation has done. We see this with Iyana Martin from Spain, MVP of the under-19 in 2023. And she signed a big sponsorship agreement herself just with a FIBA partner two days before the tournament. "So players around the world are picking up these opportunities. And I'm extremely proud of them. And I can tell you, I do believe that in the Los Angeles Olympics, our female players may be at the same or even higher level of popularity than many of our former male players. And this is not a criticism to anybody. It's just a result of the collective growth of the game. And we're proud for both the male and female players that we have to admit have made our sport as global as it is today." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Clark has become one the biggest storylines of this year's tournament, and has done so without even starting a game. Clark has come off the bench in each of Team USA's five wins, alongside fellow young stars Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers, as coach Kara Lawson has opted to play the veteran starters in all five of the U.S. wins. Still, Clark has been among the tournament's top performers. The 24-year-old guard has clocked just over 20 minutes per game, placing her among the team's most utilized players. In those minutes, she has proven to be an elite facilitator, currently ranking third in the entire World Cup with 5.8 assists per game. articles.title: Las 12 chicas de bronce
articles.standfirst: Así son y así han jugado las internacionales que han conquistado la tercera plaza del Mundial
articles.summary: Así son y así han jugado las internacionales que han conquistado la tercera plaza del Mundial
articles.body: Un equipo mayúsculo. Eso es la selección femenina que se ha colgado la medalla de bronce en el Mundial, la cuarta que consigue España en el torneo. Talento y trabajo a partes iguales, mezcla de veteranía e insultante juventud, así son y así han jugado las 12 chicas de bronce. Pura intensidad en la pista. La escolta canaria ha sido clave cuando había que apretar las tuercas un poco más. Con 1,74 metros, la más baja de la selección, aunque su estatura nunca es un obstáculo, pues lo suple con habilidad y conocimiento del juego. Tremenda intución para atrapar rebotes ofensivos pese a su falta de centímetros: xx en todo el torneo. En la semifinal ante Estados Unidos le colocó un tapón a Aliya Boston, de 1,96. Menos protagonista que en otros torneos o con el Casademont Zaragoza, donde ha alcanzado la categoría de ídolo, ha dirigido la segunda unidad siempre aportando templanza y su habitual buen criterio al timón. Con gran generosidad, la segunda jugadora más veterana de la selección ha puesto su experiencia y su talento a disposición del grupo. El metrónomo de la selección. Titular en los seis encuentros, la base canaria ha marcado el ritmo en los dos lados de la pista. Delante, con una visión de juego privilegiada. Máxima asistente y mejor ratio asistencias/pérdidas del equipo. Detrás, con una intensidad defensiva que, eso sí, en ocasiones le hace cargarse demasiado rápido de faltas. Cuarta medalla mundialista para la gran capitana. Sólo la estadounidense Sue Bird tiene más que ella. Alba cumplió 37 años durante la preparación, pero sigue al pie del cañón con un compromiso y una ilusión inquebrantables. Ha jugado menos que nadie en la selección, pero su importancia iba más allá del parqué. Entre grandes dosis de juventud, ella era la voz de la experiencia, la única que había estado en un Mundial. Su leyenda es un poco más grande. La nueva jugadora del Valencia Basket ha tenido un rol en la sombra. Casi no se ha prodigado en ataque con apenas dos tiros por encuentro. Se ha dedicado casi siempre a labores defensivas, donde ha cumplido. Una de las referencias ofensivas de la selección. Ha sido capaz de extrapolar al equipo nacional las buenas prestaciones que estaba mostrando en las Toronto Tempo de la WNBA. Numerosos recursos en ataque tanto cerca del aro, penetrando o imponiendo su talla, como desde el triple. Nexo entre las veteranas y las jóvenes, seguirá siendo clave en los próximos campeonatos. Icono de presente y futuro. Su espectacular planta y sus condiciones le hacen una jugadora como ha habido pocas en España. Quizás la única fuera Sancho Lyttle. Todo lo bueno que estaba haciendo en las Seattle Storm lo ha disfrutado ahora la selección, donde ha sido quien más tiempo ha estado en pista durante el Mundial. Intimidante en defensa y con recursos en ataque. Cerca del 40% en triples. Un poco ansiosa en algunos partidos, se le escapó más de una canasta bajo el aro. En la pelea por el bronce, 10+9. De menos a más en el Mundial. Le costó coger ritmo después de estar jugando poco en las Liberty. Sin embargo, se dejó el mejor partido para la lucha por el bronce: 15 puntos y cinco asistencias. Magnífico tercer cuarto ante Alemania. Jugadora para llevarse a una guerra, ha estado en todas las batallas. Muchas veces por el suelo peleando por un rebote o un balón suelto, bregando con las interiores rivales y a la vez mostrando su capacida ofensiva. Un pilar fundamental. Por debajo de lo esperado. De las cinco jugadoras provenientes de la WNBA, a la que más le ha costado encajar en el equipo y la que menos ha participado. Llamada a ser referencia ofensiva, ha estado irregular. En la pintura, bastante mejor que desde el perímetro. Con cada buena defensa, puño al aire. Es lo que se esperaba de ella, que apretará atrás como siempre hace. Hubo quien cuestionó su inclusión en la lista definitiva de 12 para el Mundial, pero se ha encargado con su esfuerzo de liquidar esas dudas. Jugadora de las que ayudan a ganar desde el trabajo oscuro. Sus lágrimas tras ser nombrada MVP del partido de cuartos decían mucho. La segunda internacional menos utilizada por el seleccionador Miguel Méndez, le ha tocado hacer el necesario trabajo sucio en defensa. En ataque apenas ha podido desplegar su buen tiro de media distancia. En todos los equipos se necesitan trabajadores abnegados que no reclaman protagonismo. Iyana se cayó a una marmita llena de balones cuando era pequeña y eso le otorgó poderes para hacer lo que quiera en la pista. Ha asombrado desplegando su magia en acciones que bien valen el precio de una entrada: triples a una pierna, entradas imposibles, bailes camino del aro... Una de las estrellas del torneo por lo que transmite y por juego. Para rematar, 22 puntos y nueve asistencias en la lucha por el bronce. La próxima temporada seguirá en la Liga Femenina Endesa enrolada en el Spar Girona, pero su hábitat natural es la WNBA. Las Portland Fire la seleccionaron en el séptimo lugar del draft y todo apunta a que se irá en 2027. El futuro es suyo: ¡sólo 20 años!

articles.title: Alba Torrens agranda su leyenda con su cuarta medalla mundialista
articles.standfirst: La capitana de la selección suma una plata (2014) y tres bronces (2010, 2018 y 2026) y sólo Sue Bird ha conseguido más que ella
articles.summary: La capitana de la selección suma una plata (2014) y tres bronces (2010, 2018 y 2026) y sólo Sue Bird ha conseguido más que ella
articles.body: Alba Torrens llegó a Berlín como la única jugadora española con experiencia en un Mundial. Debutó en 2010 y entonces se colgó un bronce. Jugó también el de 2014 y aquella España en la que ella estaba sólo cedió ante Estados Unidos en la final. Jugó también en 2018 y subió al tercer cajón del podio. La selección faltó a la cita en 2022 y, en su regreso, este verano, la alero ha vuelto a vestirse de bronce. Cuarta medalla en cuatro participaciones. "Es un momento muy feliz y mi felicidad va más allá de mi. Estoy feliz por el equipo, por Miguel [Méndez, el seleccionador], por el staff, por Elisa [Aguilar, presidenta de la FEB] y por la federación. Cuando tu felicidad va más allá de ti, creo que encuentras más significado y creo que lo hemos demostrado al colgarnos esta medalla de mucho valor", analizaba. El hito está a la altura de muy pocas jugadoras en la historia del baloncesto. Sólo Sue Bird, con cinco medallas mundialistas, tiene más que Torrens. Sólo estadounidenses y alguna australiana como Lauren Jackson puede presumir de llegar a las cuatro. La española, entre las leyendas. Pero las medallas mundialistas son sólo una parte de la cosecha de éxitos que Alba ha recogido durante su dilatada carrera con la selección, que incluye 11 podios: también plata en los Juegos de 2016, oros en los Eurobasket de 2013 y 2017, platas en 2023 y 2025 y bronces en 2009 y 2015. A sus 37 años, cumplidos durante la preparación del Mundial, Torrens fue incluida en la lista definitiva de la selección femenina. Su ilusión se mantenía intacta después de tantos años, en los que ha llegado a ser la sexta jugadora con más partidos internacionales con España. Después de una temporada jugando en el Azulmarino Mallorca, con el que logró el ascenso a la Liga Femenina Endesa, su convocatoria iba más allá de la pista. articles.summary: La base, elegida mejor jugadora del partido por el bronce, ha brillado en todo el Mundial
articles.body: España es un EQUIPO con mayúsculas, no hay duda. Lo recalcaban Miguel Méndez y Alba Torrens al final del partido: "El equipo ha sido la clave". Pero en ese colectivo tan sólido que ha sido la selección, ha sobresalido Iyana Martín con un brillo muy especial. La ovetense se ha presentado a mundo como una superestrella en ciernes. Ya es, por méritos propios, una de las jugadoras con mayor progresión del planeta. Iyana apareció con esa sonrisa que todo lo ilumina tras el partido con la medalla de bronce colgada al cuello que mostró a MARCA (vídeo). le costaba hablar con cierta calma porque todo era euforia. Y quiso acordarse de sus compañeras: "Ya lo dije ayer, estoy muy orgullosa de mis compañeras, del trabajo del equipo y a los hechos me remito, creo que hemos hecho una preparación y un campeonato espectacular, creo que hemos sabido crecer partido a partido y, esta medalla demuestra todo lo que hemos trabajado, lo que hemos hecho...", de pronto aparece Alicia Flórez: "¡Apártate! No tiene palabras esta chica. Es que no le podéis preguntar nada porque no tiene palabras". La buena sintonía entre ellas se respira. Iyana explica que para preparar el Mundial tuvo que renunciar a ir a la WNBA este mismo ño: "Estoy muy contenta porque tomé una decisión de no ir a la WNBA para venir bien al campeonato, creo que me ha ido bien, estoy supercontenta". Iyana ha crecido con el equipo y el equipo con ella: "Creo que el equipo en el que estoy me lo permite, creo que todos somos un equipo estupendo, que me deja ser yo misma, que me da la confianza para coger los tiros, para cometer errores y seguir siendo yo misma, entonces no puedo pedir más. Muy orgullosa de todas, porque todas han hecho posible todo lo que ha pasado durante el campeonato y nada, la verdad es que no puedo estar más contenta". Por último, la MVP de la final de consolación habló sobre el partido: "Al final creo que hemos estado muy acertadas en la toma de decisiones en general todas, creo que les hemos dificultado esa defensa, no les hemos dado ningún tipo de oportunidad de superarnos, hemos cortado el tipo de juego que ellas querían, han intentado acelerarnos en varias ocasiones y hemos aguantado como jabatas hasta el último minuto. Nos hemos vaciado, nos hemos dejado todo y al final ha visto reflejado el resultado".

articles.body: El bronce en el Mundial de Berlín ha cerrado un verano extraordinario de las selecciones femeninas de la de Federación Española de Baloncesto. Uno más, pues se trata de una factoría de conseguir éxitos en forma de medallas que hace tiempo que convirtió a España en la mayor potencia europea. Esta vez, ha habido pleno: cinco en otros tantos campeonatos. Al bronce de las mayores se suman el también tercer puesto de la selección U20 en el Eurobasket, el oro de la U18, la plata de la U17 en un Mundial donde sólo cedió frente a Estados Unidos y el oro de una U16 que domina la categoría con tremenda autoridad: son ya 20 podios de forma consecutiva. Entre los éxitos colectivos aparecen nombres que formarán parte del futuro del baloncesto español: Somto Okafor y Amelia Alonso fueron MVP de los Eurobasket U18 y U16, respectivamente, mientras que Inés Sotelo e Isabel Hernández formaron parte de los mejores quintetos del Eurobasket U20 y del Mundial U17. Todos esos triunfos invitan a pensar que el futuro sea todavía más brillante que el presente. Jugadoras de enorme talento se sumarán a las jóvenes que ya son protagonistas en la absoluta como Iyana Martín y Awa Fam, que tienen 20 años, Elena Buenavida, Alicia Flórez, Raquel Carrera...

articles.title: USA vs. France Box Score, Highlights for Clark, Reese from 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup Bracket Final
articles.summary: The entire 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup built toward Sunday's championship game between powerhouses in the United States and France, and the Americans came away with their fifth consecutive title.
articles.body:
The entire 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup built toward Sunday's championship game between powerhouses in the United States and France, and the Americans came away with their fifth consecutive title.

The Red, White and Blue defended their crown with a 97-79 victory and continued their dominance of international play that has seen them capture every Olympic and World Cup gold since 1996 except the 2006 World Cup when they ended with bronze.

Breanna Stewart and Jackie Young were brilliant, Chelsea Gray provided a steadying veteran hand, and Caitlin Clark added a spark off the bench.

Live Live: USA eyes World Cup gold vs. France

Anything but a final between the United States and France would have been surprising.

After all, these two teams played in a thriller in the gold-medal game at the 2024 Paris Olympics. The United States escaped with a one-point victory in that one, but France returned to the World Cup with Gabby Williams leading plenty of WNBA firepower on its roster.

France also steamrolled all five of its previous opponents in this tournament with a 22-point win over Germany in the semifinals as its closest game. Sunday figured to be a daunting task for a loaded United States roster that features Napheesa Collier, Young, Gray, Clark, Paige Bueckers, Stewart, Angel Reese and more.

With Williams spearheading the attack with her drives and outside shooting, France extended its lead to double digits in the second quarter. However, the Americans bounced right back behind the trio of Stewart, Young and Gray.

Young caught fire from deep, Gray did a little bit of everything with her facilitating and drives, and Stewart was a matchup problem in the lane. By the time Clark drilled a three in the final seconds before intermission, the United States had cut the halftime deficit to just two points and seemed to have weathered a significant storm from France.

That momentum went nowhere during the break.

Veterans such as Stewart, Collier and Kahleah Copper were dominant on both ends of the floor before one of the youngsters in Clark hit a jumper right at the buzzer to give the Americans a 16-point lead heading into the fourth.

They outscored France 30-12 in the third behind suffocating defense and a balanced scoring attack. It was the type of performance one might expect from a group of WNBA stars, and Clark kept it rolling with an early three in the fourth quarter.

It reached a point where there was very little drama in the fourth quarter.

While it seemed like France was going to hand the United States a shocking loss in the first half, the dialed up defensive pressure along with the efficient offense with so many players contributing overwhelmed the challengers.

France simply didn't have the depth of starpower as the Americans, and the result was the gold medal staying with the Red, White and Blue.

articles.title: Estados Unidos gana a Francia y mantiene intacto el orden mundial
articles.standfirst: En la final sufrió menos que contra Italia o España y acaba llevándose su quinto oro consecutivo
articles.summary: En la final sufrió menos que contra Italia o España y acaba llevándose su quinto oro consecutivo
articles.body: Estados Unidos le debe una muy gorda a Breanna Stewart y a Jackie Young. En el momento más crítico del partido, cuando Francia se exhibía y se escapaba, 22-33, aparecieron las dos para rescatar a un equipo que, si no ha perdido en este Mundial, igual no pierde ya jamás. Stewart sí partía entre la lista de estrellas del equipo pero Young, gran jugadora, estaba tapada por el fulgor de otras como Clark, Gray, Bueckers o Reese, que han estado muy por debajo de su nivel en este Mundial. En la lista de las salvadoras de EEUU habría que añadir a Aliyah Boston, no tanto por su final ante Francia, y sí por el rendimiento que tuvo ante España. Las tres, de alguna forma u otra, han puesto a buen recaudo la historia de una dominación absoluta que sigue creciendo: casi 20 años sin perder (el 21 de septiembre los hace) y 72 partidos seguidos ganados en Juegos Olímpicos y Mundiales. Sorpresivamente, la final fue menos traumática para EEUU, 97-79, que su partido ante Italia o la semifinal frente a España. En esos partidos, transalpinas y españolas las llevaron al límite e incluso merecieron mejor suerte. Frente a Francia, que se mostró mucho mejor que las norteamericanas en todo el torneo, el encuentro fue más plácido una vez pasado el susto cuando faltaban 6:30 para el descanso y ganaba Francia, 22-33. Ni la gran Gabby Williams, con 20 puntos y muy ovacionada cuando se fue al final, ni Salaun ni Malonga ni Johannes pudieron parar el vendaval estadounidense tras el descanso al que se llegó 43-45 para las galas. Desde ahí, un 30-12 de parcial en el tercer cuarto dejó el choque casi sentenciado a falta de todo un periodo: 73-57. En ese último acto la ventaja americana creció hasta una máxima de 27 puntos (86-59). Un arranque de orgullo francés impidió un marador más duro, pero hacía muchos minutos que la final ya se había acabado. La fama de Francia de bloquearse en los momentos culminantes de los torneos volvió a aflorar. De verdad que en la expedición francesa existía la creencia de que se ganaría la final. En un sólo cuarto se esfumó el sueño y la corona fue a parar al equipo que la ha estado llevando desde 2010. Breanna Stewart se fue en la final a un doble-doble de 22 puntos y 10 rebotes. Es una garantía absoluta y si el mundo no ha visto en Berlín una derrota de EEUU es en gran parte por ella. Jackie Young acabó con 18 en una actuación sublime, su mejor partido en un torneo muy regular. Y hasta Caitlin Clark brilló con 12 puntos anotando cuando su equipo tenía amarrado el título. La de las Fever tendrá mucho en qué pensar dado su bajísimo rendimiento en todo el campeonato. En Francia, además de Williams, Malonga hizo 21 puntos y, como es habitual en las galas, se produjo un colapso colectivo en el resto. Tampoco es mal premio para las francesas la primera final de su historia y la segunda medalla, la primera de plata, después dl bronce que ganaron en 1953 en Chile que ya se ha perdido en la noche de los tiempos. La de Berlín tiene mucho más brillo.

articles.title: "Las medallas alegran, pero en un mes estarán colgando de un ganchito. Me quedo con el camino"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador femenino Miguel Méndez analiza el éxito del bronce en el Mundial
articles.summary: El seleccionador femenino Miguel Méndez analiza el éxito del bronce en el Mundial
articles.body: Miguel Méndez cosechó un nuevo éxito que mejora una ya extraordinaria carrera. El seleccionador nacional consiguió su segunda medalla con España. Tras la plata del Eurobasket del verano pasado en una final en la que se escapó el oro, llega un bronce que sabe muy dulce. Antes ya había triunfado a nivel de clubes, con cuatro Euroligas ganadas entre el Ekaterinburg y el Fenerbahce. Con el bronce al cuello, Méndez se enorgullecía por "haberlo hecho con un equipo joven, que ha sabido equilibrar los dos estilos de juego. Hemos sabido ser un grupo humano más allá de las individualidades. Hemos superado la vida misma, porque las jugadoras han llegado en diferentes momentos, de diferente forma física. Todas han sabido adaptarse". De todo el campeonato, recurriendo al clásico, se queda "con el camino. Ha sido una vez más increíble, el día a día, este mes y medio fuera de casa, pero encontrarte a gusto en todo momento". El seleccionador considera que "las medallas alegran, pero en un mes estarán colgando de un ganchito. Las personas y los momentos, en cambio, quedan”. Entre esas personas, quienes se colgaron la medalla este domingo, pero también quienes ayudaron a conseguirlo desde la sombra o las jugadoras que fueron descartadas. A todos ellos les recordó Méndez: "Estoy contento con el trabajo que hacen los entrenadores, los clubes, las Federaciones. Hay mucha gente detrás. Los primeros entrenadores de Iyana, que no sé cómo se llaman, los que ha tenido. Los que estamos ahora disfrutamos de ella. Hay que ponderar el trabajo que se hace". La unión del equipo se demostró con la visita sorpresa de Andrea Vilaró poco antes de la lucha por el bronce. "Fue uno de los últimos descartes. Jugó ayer la final de la Copa de Galicia y hoy ha aparecido por la mañana cuando estaban haciendo los ejercicios de estiramiento. Ha sido un empujón moral. Y es un detalle que marca lo que somos, no solo las 12, sino muchos más”, finalizó el técnico.

articles.title: With fifth straight FIBA World Cup title, Team USA bridges past, present and future to uphold gold standard
articles.summary: In what was rightfully billed as their toughest challenge, Team USA looked every bit as worthy of the world domination title they've maintained for more than...
articles.body:
And so the standard strengthens once more.

In what was rightfully billed as their toughest challenge, and after falling behind by as many as 14 in the gold medal match to France, Team USA looked every bit as worthy of the world domination title they've maintained for more than three decades. Even if, through much of the tournament, they clung perilously to the claim.

They nearly lost to Italy in the group stage. They struggled against bronze medalist Spain in the semifinals . The rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold medal game against France proved difficult in a disjointed start that could have spiraled.

That's not the Team USA standard. No matter the increasing strength of international talent, or the experience on their own bench, they level up to the moment. Only gold will do.

To fall short is not simply about a different medal color. It's a failure to the crest, and to oneself, as the names who allowed the program to falter. That goes for newly minted four-time champion Breanna Stewart to burgeoning stars Caitlin Clark , Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers on down to late additions Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron . All lived up to the assignment in a 97-79 statement on the international stage.

Stewart steadied the squad again on Sunday, playing the increasingly necessary role of bridge between Team USA of rosters past and the glutton of talent poised to take charge by the next World Cup cycle. She is undefeated in NCAA, Olympic and World Cup championship games. She lost only one of her four WNBA Finals appearances.

The future Hall of Famer earned a record-setting second World Cup MVP honor after 22 points and 10 rebounds. She was the first U.S. player this tournament to crack 20 points and averaged a team-high 12.8 points and 7.3 rebounds per game.

Jackie Young added to a uniquely deep trophy case by adding 18 points in the gold medal game. Veterans Kahleah Copper (15 points, 5 of 9) and Chelsesa Gray (12 points, 5 of 9) cracked double digits, with Gray adding four rebounds and five assists in primary point guard duties. Clark scored 12 on an efficient 4 of 5 in 13 minutes.

It took a little from everyone to turn a 14-point deficit into a 27-point lead. Head coach Kara Lawson put her veteran starters back in at 8:08 of the second to avoid the collapse, and with Aliyah Boston inserted into the lineup as the team's center, they came within five with 29 seconds until half.

Lawson, whose lineup decisions were suspect at times, put in Reese for Boston to get a stop. The Dream forward pressured Liberty guard Pauline Astier, forcing the turnover. Lawson swapped out Reese for Clark, who drained the buzzer-beating 3-pointer to make it a one-possession game. Clark hit another quarter-ending jumper to close out the third. They were Team USA's 30th points, capping a 30-12 frame that all but officially slammed the door on revenge-hungry France.

And by extension, the rest of the world.

No one is going to feel sorry for the powerhouse that won all but one World Cup or Olympic gold medal since 1996 (they lost the 2006 World Cup). They entered this tournament having won four consecutive World Cup golds since that loss, and came into the final on a 36-game World Cup winning streak.

The history doesn't discredit how much was stacked against Team USA in the present. Those who looked at the final score or watched the second half will insist France was never a true threat. Hindsight is 20/20. There was plenty of reason to believe this was the competition that could finally trip up the Americans.

More than any previous senior tournament in recent memory, this cycle's team was composed of two distinct and separate parts compiled by first-ever managing director and four-time World Cup medalist Sue Bird.

In one camp were the five veterans of senior-level competition — only three from the previous World Cup gold after A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum were unavailable on the eve of the tournament. In another, a crop of young headline talent inexperienced at the senior level.

They played two distinct styles for a collegiate head coach in Duke's Lawson, who specifically took a WNBA color analyst job to see her players throughout the summer. No matchup showcased this better than Spain, as the veterans struggled a step behind and the young crew dug out of the hole by keeping and setting pace.

It was hard to meld those two versions together. The team did not have a proper training camp, an aspect that will change come 2030 when the tournament is held in November/December after the WNBA season concludes. Instead, it fell to a FIBA World Cup qualifying tournament roster in March. The time gave the young stars runway to develop on the international level, but not time to build chemistry with the key standard-bearing veterans.

Stewart joined the team for a pre-competition training camp, but did not compete. Wilson also did not attend. The co-face of Team USA's current iteration alongside Stewart, she backed out of the World Cup to get healthy back home for a WNBA championship run with the Las Vegas Aces . Plum helmed the backcourt as the third-leading scorer in Puerto Rico, but also could not head to Germany with lingering leg injuries.

Napheesa Collier was sidelined after surgeries on both of her ankles after last season, and only returned to basketball action in July. She mishandled a few of Clark's dagger passes while cutting in the paint, eliciting memories of how Iowa players learned to keep their heads on a swivel early in Clark's collegiate career. Those are the slight misses that strengthen with time the team didn't have.

Not to mention the world is no longer star-struck by the mighty Americans, whose armor is melting with each national team that stays close late and every star who signs with the WNBA. The World Cup field featured 70 current and former WNBA players, including 58 rostered outside of Team USA. Puerto Rico was the only team without an active WNBA player.

Eight of France's 12 players are on WNBA rosters, and another two played previously in the best league in the world. They carried experience with one another, established understandings of Team USA's looming threats, and a healthy hunger from falling a few inches short of overtime in the 2024 Paris Olympic gold medal game.

None of that ended up mattering. Gabby Williams , the third-highest scorer in the tournament, didn't score in the second half until 1:45 left in the game. She finished with 20 and Dominique Malonga with 21 as the only double-digit French players. They couldn't capitalize on Team USA's early turnovers and collapsed once Team USA gritted its way to the proper footing.

Stewart, 32, emphatically told the broadcast to expect her at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in what would be her fourth appearance. The roster will look similar to this one, with a heavy emphasis on the young crew, though the hurdles it faced will be a thing of the past.

If the acclaimed "Young and Turnt" crew learned anything at all in Berlin, it's the heavy first-hand burden that Team USA finds a way. To reach the final game is what matters. To stand atop the podium above everyone else is not the goal. It's the expectation.

That standard is a skill they had yet to add to a formidable Team USA bag. Now, the standard continues.

articles.title: Florida guard Denzel Aberdeen sues the NCAA in hopes of gaining a fifth year of eligibility
articles.summary: Florida guard Denzel Aberdeen has joined a growing list of players suing the NCAA in hopes of gaining a fifth year of eligibility.
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Florida guard Denzel Aberdeen has joined a growing list of players suing the NCAA in hopes of gaining a fifth year of eligibility.

Aberdeen's attorney, Jesse Panuccio, filed the lawsuit Friday in Gainesville. His motion notes that more than 30 courts across the country have ruled that the NCAA's "arbitrary decision" against student-athletes who began college careers during the 2022-23 season and completed four seasons of eligibility is "unlawful."

"The NCAA's refusal to honor its current eligibility framework breaches its contract with UF, which is intended to benefit student-athletes like Aberdeen," the suit said.

The NCAA's move to a five-year, age-based eligibility model has led to a series of court fights across the country.

Aberdeen played three seasons at Florida before transferring to Kentucky last year. He reenrolled at Florida earlier this year in hopes of finishing his undergraduate degree. He has worked out and practiced with the Gators all summer.

He initially planned to convince the NCAA that his freshman year in Gainesville should be considered a redshirt season. The 6-foot-5 Orlando native played just 12 games in 2022-23, scoring 19 points in 41 total minutes. He had hoped to get a waiver from the NCAA to secure another year of eligibility.

But the NCAA has since adopted the five-year eligibility model, which is scheduled to be fully implemented next fall, that will allow players to have five years of eligibility with the clock starting when athletes turn 19 or graduate from high school, whichever is earlier.

That change quickly led to lawsuits from four-year players in the high school class of 2022, like Aberdeen.

As of last week, the NCAA said there have been 79 lawsuits with a total of 450 plaintiffs across all sports involved in litigation tied to the five-year rule, with 234 of those coming in men's basketball and 33 in women's basketball. Of that group, 154 men's players and 26 women's players have received some type of relief from the courts allowing them to play while the rest are currently ineligible.

If granted a temporary restraining order, Aberdeen would slide into a starting spot to replace Xaivian Lee.

The Gators already are the betting favorite — and likely to be ranked No. 1 in preseason polls — to win it all in 2027. Coach Todd Golden retained most of last year's roster, most notably big men Alex Condon, Thomas Haugh and Rueben Chinyelu.

Aberdeen started 35 games for Kentucky last season, averaging 13.5 points, 3.4 assists and 2.5 rebounds. He came off the bench the previous two years at Florida and averaged 7.7 points as a junior in 2024-25.
